attacks.target_position: Vulkan engineer: raw Win32 through windows-sys is the better window and input layer
attacks.finding: The technical reasons fail against the locked source. winit 0.30.13 already handles WM_POINTER with frame history and pen pressure, uses the same IMM32 calls proposed, does SetCapture on press, and catches panics around every callback. Only two things are missing: tilt, and PT_PEN arrives as Touch. with_msg_hook sees each queued MSG before dispatch, so tilt and pen history can come from GetPointerPenInfoHistory in about 60 lines in the leaf (ESTIMATE, not exercised). The render-thread argument does not separate them either: a render thread with the raw HWND works under winit. Cost side: winit's Windows backend is 9,625 lines, 2,229 of them keyboard and layouts, against the engineer's 'few thousand' and a 5-commit lane that lists keyboard, pen, IME, DPI, cursors, clipboard, AccessKit and multiwindow. A raw WndProc is unsafe code where a panic through extern system aborts the process, and SetWindowPos inside WM_DPICHANGED re-enters it. First-party quiet proof exists only for winit: KUM native.rs creates windows with_visible(false), with_active(false), sets WS_EX_NOACTIVATE through the raw handle, and its README records 22 hidden native captures and six UIA stages. GPUI being winit-free shows it can be done by a team whose product is that layer; it says nothing about one night here. Pick: winit. It saves about one lane (ESTIMATE) and removes the input-corner defect class, at the price of a thin hook for tilt.
evidence: Line counts of src/platform_impl/windows: total 9625; keyboard.rs 1243, keyboard_layout.rs 986
KUM kumihimo-egui/src/native.rs:1172-1173, :3206-3223; kumihimo-egui/Cargo.toml feature native; product/README.md lines 29, 44, 46
attacks.what_to_decide_instead: winit =0.30.13 plus windows-sys in hsk-studio-native-host only. The typed HostEvent queue from the engineer's position stays, so a Win32 backend can replace winit later by editing one crate.

attacks.target_position: Raw Vulkan overnight with no validation layer: where it actually bites
attacks.finding: The concrete failure is not corruption on screen. It is the GPU test lock. Three predicates key on render-gpu only: studio-env.sh takes the lock for `--workspace` or render-gpu selections, run-round's crate_gpu returns 1 only for render-gpu, and the nextest test-group filter is package(hsk-studio-render-gpu). New Vulkan crates would run unlocked at test-threads 8 beside a round's GPU units, and `studio-vk offscreen` runs are not nextest at all. R39 already showed the result of foreign GPU clients: 22 render-gpu TIMEOUTs, class gpu_contention_foreign_clients. Two rounds of that class trigger CX-EXEC-015(4), no round on those MTs until a pushed config commit. A bad raw submit that resets the driver would also reach the Operator's Chrome (blast radius UNVERIFIED). Next: NVIDIA tolerates wrong layouts and missing barriers, so tonight's green means little on other GPUs, and there is no other GPU here. An unbounded fence wait hangs a builder while it holds the lock.
evidence: P .config/nextest.toml test-threads = 8, filter package(hsk-studio-render-gpu), R39 comment
attacks.what_to_decide_instead: Steward adds the new Vulkan crates to all three predicates, plus a wrapper for host binary runs, before any Vulkan lane runs a test. Stand-ins until the layer exists: first window is transfer and present only, with no pipeline or descriptor; vkDeviceWaitIdle before every swapchain recreate; semaphores per swapchain image; every fence wait bounded and typed; naga validation plus a spv-in reparse in the tool; pixel compare of Vulkan against the CPU painter; receipt field validation: absent. The profile is in unit_id, so adoption is the forced rebuild, whenever it happens: 13 to 30 minutes per target, 3 to 6 lock-hours across 12, losing exactly the compile reuse HSK-ART-005 asks for. Tonight it buys nothing urgent: C: has 403 GB free and D: 1,205 GB. The probe is up to 45 lock-minutes on D: during the first wave, a 7th target there, for a result that cannot be adopted tonight. Also, research says run-round must refuse CARGO_TARGET_*_LINKER before any lane adopts, or CX-VAL-007 breaks; Delivery's plan omits that guard. Merging test binaries after R60 is right, but its real cost is larger than stated: required_proof keys in every verdict use binary names, 797 --test references need a map, the ladder Delivery just wrote names --test files, and one full round costs about 4 to 6 h. Do it before panel fan-out, since panel lanes convert tests.
evidence: S/research/cargo-reuse-research-20261107.json Q2 'Profile is in unit_id', Q3 failure_modes env leak, Q4 risks
attacks.what_to_decide_instead: No probe, debug=0 or linker change tonight. Put the run-round linker guard in the steward sync, since R60 is FULL anyway. After R60: probe, then adopt both settings in one rebuild per target. Merge harness-view then harness in that same quiet gap.

attacks.target_position: Delivery: Plan R 'prune first on C:', 'D: rows at background rate'

The first wave is writing into those D: targets now, so those rows need the Operator, who is asleep. Pruned rows also relink on first use just as the C: window opens.
